precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war; contests of strength were known among His people.
precepts.point: When Asahel refused to turn aside, Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear under the fifth rib, and he died there. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. Those who came to the place stood still; the lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.”

At the pool of Gibeon, Abner said to Joab, “Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.” To play there means to compete and battle one another. The Lord is a man of war, and contests of strength like this were known among his people and done in that day.

Twelve of Benjamin and twelve of David’s servants “caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together”, and that place was called Helkath-hazzurim. Then “there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.”

Asahel, “as light of foot as a wild roe”, meaning he was fast, pursued Abner and would not turn aside, though Abner warned him again and again: “wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?” When he refused, Abner smote him “with the hinder end of the spear” under the fifth rib, “that the spear came out behind him”. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. As many as came to the place stood still. The lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

points: David inquired of the Lord whether he should go up into any of the cities of Judah, and the Lord said, Go up, unto Hebron. David did not move to take the kingdom until he asked whether it was time to be king.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: David went up with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite, and with every man and his household, and they dwelt in the cities of Hebron.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: The men of Judah came and there anointed David king over the house of Judah. He was raised up because the Most High had anointed him to be the next king over Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: David sent to the men of Jabeshgilead who had buried Saul, blessing them for the kindness shown to their lord, and telling them Judah had anointed him king over them.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ishbosheth the son of Saul and made him king over Gilead and Israel; Ishbosheth was forty years old and reigned two years, while Judah followed David. David reigned in Hebron over Judah seven years and six months.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner and the servants of Ishbosheth met Joab and the servants of David at the pool of Gibeon, sitting on opposite sides. Abner said, Let the young men arise and play, meaning let them compete and battle one another; the Lord is a man of war, and such contests were done in that day.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Twelve of Benjamin and twelve of David's servants caught each his fellow by the head and thrust the sword in his fellow's side, so they fell down together, and that place was called Helkathhazzurim. Abner and the men of Israel were beaten before the servants of David.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Asahel, one of the three sons of Zeruiah, was as light of foot as a wild roe, meaning he was fast, and he pursued Abner and would not turn aside. Abner warned him again and again to turn off and take another man's armor, not wanting to have to kill him and face Joab his brother.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: When Asahel refused to turn aside, Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear under the fifth rib, and he died there. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. Those who came to the place stood still; the lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Joab and Abishai pursued Abner until sundown, and the children of Benjamin gathered to Abner in one troop and stood on the top of a hill. Abner had rounded up his men and stood ready.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner called to Joab, asking whether the sword should devour forever, and warned that it would be bitterness in the latter end; he asked how long before Joab bade the people return from following their brethren. Joab answered that unless Abner had spoken, the people would have gone up in the morning, and he blew the trumpet and the people stood still and fought no more.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

points: Abner and his men walked all that night and came to Mahanaim. Of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel were missing, but they had smitten of Abner's men three hundred and threescore. They buried Asahel at Bethlehem, and Joab and his men came to Hebron at break of day.
